hypothesis: UHS-I SDR104 (profile 3) lifetime B on port 3-3 in the returning image switches to 1.8 V, tunes and reads.
conclusion:
The failed step was 1. The core waited for command done after CMD11 (drivers/storage/sunxi_mmc.c, command step 2), as for every other command. The controller had reported CMD11 with bit 10 and withholds command done until step 6, which the core never reached, so the wait ran until the identification deadline. The emulation's card model had reported command done at CMD11, so the checks passed. State left: the PF bank stayed at 3.3 V; no error or timeout bit was set, so the card most likely answered CMD11 and then drove its lines low waiting for the clock to stop. The clock ran at the identification rate until the image's clock stop gated the module clock, 1.16 s after start. A card that had accepted CMD11 may then have switched its outputs to 1.8 V while the bank stayed at 3.3 V; the specification allows only a power cycle to leave this state (C:1262-1265), so whole-board power removal is the recovery.
Fix (driver and emulation): CMD11 completes on bit 10 and reads its R1 then, with nothing else checked after it, as in the vendor driver (sunxi_mmc.c, command steps 2 and 3). After the clock restart the core clears every flag the update set, as the vendor does after each clock update (V:386-388), and the switch ends only on DAT3 high with both bit 10 and command done arriving afterwards (sd_signal, steps 4 and 5), as K:2296-2307 requires. The returning image's clock stop carries VOLTAGE_SWITCH while a switch is in progress (V:378-379). checks/storage-read-sd-modes.py's UHS card model reports CMD11 as the board did, and the switch's end only after the clock restart; checks/storage-read-returning.py profile 3 passes with the fix, and the image of set 28 stops in that model at CMD11, as on the board. The fix then ran on port 3-3: 1793648082135831049-05f70d50 completed the CMD11 switch and 32 reads (its close failed for an unrelated filter rule), and the SDR104 lifetime 1793650532228649180-1fb49397 ran at 150 MHz.
narrative:
Run board-session-20261025-32/port-3-3/sd-ret-b (no queue entry); lifetime A (high speed, board-session-20261025-30/port-3-3/sd-ret-a) is the record sd-dma-lifetime-a. The user approved switching the microSD signalling to 1.8 V on 2026-10-25. The image stopped after 1.16 s, before any read. The report, decoded from the code:
| Field | Value | Meaning |
| SD_REASON, SD_STAGE | 3, 1 | The provider returned RETAINED while the image polled identification (apps/storage-read-returning/main.c, stop(3)); reason 3 covers every identification failure, including the fabric refusal |
| SD_PLATFORM_STAGE, SD_PLATFORM_FAULT | 0xd, 1 | Stage IDENTIFY; the provider failed at its identification deadline (1.15 s) |
| SD_SIGNAL | 0 | The PF selector was never written; the bank stayed at 3.3 V |
| SD_CORE_STATE, SD_RESULT_ERROR | 1, 0 | The core was still identifying and had not faulted |
| SD_CORE_COMMAND, SD_CORE_ARGUMENT | 0x9000014b, 0 | CMD11 with START, VOLTAGE_SWITCH (bit 28), CRC and response |
| SD_CORE_PROTOCOL, SD_CORE_STEP | 0x1b, 2 | P_SD_VOLTAGE, waiting for the command's completion bits |
| SD_RESULT_INTERRUPTS | 0x10400 | Raw interrupts: voltage switch (bit 10) and SDIO (bit 16); no command done (bit 2), no error |
| SD_RESULT_STATUS | 0x1f906 | Read before CMD11 was written: response index 0x3f (ACMD41's R3), DAT3 high, FIFO empty, no busy |
| SD_RESULT_RESPONSE | 0x120 | The last response the core stored: CMD55's R1 (APP_CMD, READY_FOR_DATA), not CMD11's |
| SD_CLOCK_OFF | 3 | The clock update did not complete; the module clock was gated |
Reference sequence step by step (K = board kernel bsp/drivers/mmc/sunxi-mmc.c, V = sunxi-mmc-v5p3x.c, H = sunxi-mmc.h, C = drivers/mmc/core/core.c, at 2ac08e8c; mainline core.c at v6.12 has the same lines): (1) CMD11: the core sends it with R1 (C:1220-1226); the host adds VOLTAGE_SWITCH (bit 28) and masks only the errors and the voltage-switch bit 10 (K:2656-2659); the interrupt handler finishes the request when a done bit is set, the done bits include bit 10 (K:1333-1338, H:221-223), command done is not unmasked for CMD11, so CMD11 completes on bit 10, which the handler clears by writing the bits back (K:1345). (2) DAT[3:0] low: the core waits 1 ms and requires the card busy (C:1235-1239); the host's busy check reads DAT3 low while switching (K:2291-2311). (3) Card clock stop: mmc_host_set_uhs_voltage sets the clock to 0 (C:1190-1192); the host's clock update carries VOLTAGE_SWITCH and masks DAT0 (V:364-379). (4) 1.8 V: PF pin state and selector change (K:2161-2246; on this board GPIO_POW_VAL_SET_CTL). (5) Clock gated at least 10 ms, then restarted (C:1194-1200), again with VOLTAGE_SWITCH in the update (V:378-379). (6) DAT[3:0] high, 1 ms later (C:1250-1258): the host's busy check waits up to 10 ms for both bit 10 and command done (H:226-227, K:2283-2311); command done arrives only here, at the end of the switch. (7) Failure after CMD11 power-cycles the card (C:1262-1265).

hypothesis: Descriptor-free programmed-I/O reads at SDR104 150 MHz are no slower than at high speed 50 MHz, and gain at most 1.2 times.
prediction:
Goal: sequential and random read throughput in MB/s (10^6 bytes per second) from the native per-read time. The same image and card run first in profile 2 (high speed, 50 MHz, 3.3 V) and then in profile 3. The launcher's plan reads 128 consecutive 4 KiB requests, 96 4 KiB requests at fixed pseudo-random 4 KiB-aligned offsets and 32 single sectors; the single-sector reads give the per-request cost, and the difference from the 4 KiB mean gives the per-block cost.
Each 4 KiB request is one CMD18 with automatic CMD12, then CMD13. Two unmeasured costs: a guarded register access through the platform (about 0.6-1.0 us, extrapolated from the PMIC adapter's measured 0.42-0.5 us plus the time and task checks), and one FIFO word load (assumed 0.10-0.25 us). A request costs about 50-110 us of commands and platform polls, the card's first-block latency (assumed 100 us sequential, 300 us random), and per block the larger of the bus time and the PIO time.
| Per 512-byte block | High speed, 50 MHz | SDR104, 150 MHz |
| Bus time | 20.8 us | 6.9 us |
| PIO time, 128 loads and two accesses | 14-34 us | 14-34 us |
| Prediction | High speed | SDR104 |
| Sequential 4 KiB reads | 8.5-13.0 MB/s | 8.5-15.6 MB/s |
| Random 4 KiB reads | 6.0-7.9 MB/s | 6.0-8.9 MB/s |
| Per-block cost | 20.8-34 us | 14-34 us |
The programmed I/O path limits the gain to 1.0-1.2 times for sequential and 1.0-1.12 times for random reads, against the bus's 3 times. If the SDR104 per-block cost equals the high-speed one, PIO bounds both and the next change is descriptor DMA with larger requests (sd-dma). Acceptance: SDR104 throughput at least the high-speed throughput in both patterns, with identical sector digests; an unexplained shortfall blocks the merge.
Other budgets: identification: the switch takes 13-23 ms; tuning issues about 520 CMD19 (20 for each passing delay, one for each failing delay) at about 1.6 per tick plus up to 2 ms per failing delay, 0.4-0.6 s; sessions allow up to 10 s and the runbook uses 5 s. CPU: the 1 ms read budget keeps the MMC task busy for each read's duration in profiles 1-3, at most about 0.7 ms per 4 KiB read; profile 0 keeps one poll per tick. Memory: struct sunxi_mmc grows by 136 bytes (16 in the card record), struct a733_mmc_platform by 160 bytes, each read-service client slot by 12 bytes; sunxi_mmc_init's frame grows from 864 to 992 bytes (AArch64, -O2) and command_step from 560 to 576 bytes.
conclusion: Not run in this form: the board comparison used the descriptor-DMA probe instead. SDR104 at 150 MHz measured 47.6 MB/s per request and 27.4 MB/s sustained on port 3-3 (entry 1793650532228649180-1fb49397). The programmed-I/O model is superseded by the DMA read path of the sd-dma design.
narrative: Model derived before any SDR104 board run from the high-speed per-request and per-block costs of lifetime A (record sd-dma-lifetime-a).

hypothesis: The UHS-I core, platform and probe changes pass the host checks and leave the other images unchanged.
narrative:
Host checks: checks/sunxi-mmc-uhs.py pins the references by SHA-256 and asserts the cited facts, then runs two models under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. checks/sunxi-mmc-uhs.c drives the MMC core against a modeled UHS-I card: the switch order and its 1 ms and 10 ms waits, SDR104 at 150 and 100 MHz, the window rules, eight declines or fallbacks and eight terminal failures. checks/a733-mmc-uhs.c runs the actual storage platform and shared providers: one selector write in adaptive mode, both rates, no write in manual mode, a bank timeout and three losses after the switch, each retained. checks/storage-read-uhs-host.py decodes version-4 records with the unchanged observer, accepts eight consistent records and refuses ten inconsistent ones, and checks the throughput plan and summary. The existing core, write, SD-mode, idle-timing, platform, adaptive-voltage, ROM-pin, SDC3 and storage-update checks pass unchanged. The native SD-read emulation checks fail on the image before reaching this change (a repeated structure name with two layouts in the DWARF); the same check fails identically on the base image.
Integration gate sd-uhs-1025-b4bc04d0 passed on the clean tree at b4bc04d0: the storage-maintenance, board, mimus-native, GPU render, HDMI, camera and storage-probe images, the supervised OS image and the check index. Evidence: ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gate-sd-uhs-1025-b4bc04d0/ and ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/sd-uhs-20261025/ (host checks, image comparison, standalone objects of the reviewed revision in review-fixes/).
Images built from clean archives of 3c17aeca and b4bc04d0 at one shared path differ as follows:
| Image | Change |
| Read-only SD service (sunstone-a733-storage-read) | .text +7,380 B, .rodata +296 B, .bss +192 B: the UHS-I core and platform functions, the filters and the record |
| Storage maintenance | .text +6,144 B, .rodata +296 B, .bss +128 B: the same core and platform code |
| Stage-2 slot loader (a733-stage2) | .text +152 B and .bss +128 B with SUNXI_MMC_NO_UHS: larger protocol, command_step and sunxi_mmc_init from the shared structure and the high-speed refactor; no UHS-I function remains |
| Board, mimus-native, GPU render, HDMI, camera, supervised and resident OS | only the 32-byte build identity in .rodata; .text identical, because their links discard the MMC code |
The standalone single-core SD and eMMC read projects fail to link on both revisions in the board application's TinyUSB sources. Their storage objects compile on both; against the base, the eMMC build's native.c grows from 7,324 to 7,436 B and its sunxi_mmc.c from 11,758 to 17,248 B, and the single-core SD build's native.c from 7,348 to 7,704 B.
Behaviour changes from the high-speed path that the profile 3 design now includes: ACMD41 carried no S18R and a response with bit 24 faulted; CMD11 was refused by the native filter; RINTSTS bit 10 was always terminal; the PF bank had read-only checks of 3.3 V; CMD6 used function 1 only; the module clock was PERI0_400M / 4..32; sampling used the new mode with fixed phases; the read threshold was the reset value; the data timeout was 0xffffffff throughout. The read-only SD service: negotiated profiles poll an active read for up to 1 ms in one wake, as USB0 does within its 200 us budget, so each read's time measures the controller path rather than tick pacing; this applies to profiles 1 and 2 as well, so the high-speed reads are a fair comparison, while profile 0 and the eMMC build keep one poll per tick. Records are version 4: fact words 6 and 7 carry the read's elapsed microseconds and the UHS-I state, and the divisor byte's bit 7 marks the 300 MHz parent. The supervised launcher has a read-only throughput plan.
